item.text: {"search_note":"I did not find a clean 2024 before/after dataset showing nationwide changes in political violence, communal violence, deaths, injuries, or displacement under Srettha. The available evidence is mostly event-based: one de-escalatory border crisis on the positive side, and protest repression / custody abuse / southern-border impunity on the negative side. That means the overall safety judgment has to rest on qualitative balance, not on a measurable nationwide trend.","evidence":[{"title":"ASEAN Foreign Ministers’ Statement on the Escalation of Conflicts in Myanmar","publisher":"Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand","date":"2024-04-18","url":"https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/asean-fm-statement-escalation-conflicts-myanmar?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683e","summary":"Thailand joined ASEAN’s call for immediate cessation of violence, utmost restraint, humanitarian access, and protection of civilians along the Thailand-Myanmar border. The article points to selective punishment and continuing insecurity for critics.","question_ids":["3B.10","3B.8","3B.9"]},{"title":"Thailand: Last-Ditch Effort for Tak Bai Massacre Justice","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024-05-01","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/05/01/thailand-last-ditch-effort-tak-bai-massacre-justice","summary":"HRW said successive Thai governments failed to prosecute officials responsible for deaths and injuries of ethnic Malay Muslim protesters in Tak Bai. That is strong evidence of persistent impunity for communal/security-force violence, undercutting any claim of broad domestic safety gains.","question_ids":["3B.10","3B.7","3B.9"]}]}
